# Cyber Library

**Cyber Library** is a community-maintained knowledge base for cybersecurity. It brings together foundations, offensive and defensive practice, governance, intelligence, and career guidance in one structured repository, published at [cyberlibrary.fr](https://www.cyberlibrary.fr).

## What’s in this repository

The Cyber Library is organized into various categories covering different areas of cybersecurity, including:

| Section | Focus |
|--------|--------|
| [Foundation](foundation/index.mdx) | History, ethics, risk, and the human side of security |
| [Offensive](offensive/index.mdx) | Ethical hacking, testing, and adversarial simulation |
| [Defensive](defensive/index.mdx) | Monitoring, incident response, and resilience |
| [Governance](governance/index.mdx) | Policy, compliance, and executive-level security |
| [Intelligence](intelligence/index.mdx) | Threat intelligence and OSINT |
| [Career](career/index.mdx) | Roles, skills, certifications, and growth |


## Use it locally

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Cyber-Courses/Cyber-Library.git
cd Cyber-Library
```

Browse the markdown files in your editor or feed them into your own static site pipeline.

## Contribute

- **[Collaboration Wiki](https://github.com/Cyber-Courses/Cyber-Library/wiki)** — how to propose and submit content, style expectations, and review flow.
- **[Content development dashboard](https://github.com/orgs/Cyber-Courses/projects/1)** — backlog, in progress, and published work across the org.
- **Issues** — use the templates under `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` for bugs, content requests, or wiki changes.

Discussion and quick help: [Discord](https://discord.gg/a9XwRKxdHf).
